coreIdeas.mentalMove: A manager who internalizes the two-axis frame can diagnose a conversation by behavior, not by intention. The useful question becomes whether the other person received both care and clarity.
coreIdeas.name: two-axis trust
coreIdeas.oneSentence: Managerial trust forms when personal concern and direct challenge are present together. Either axis alone distorts feedback: warmth without challenge hides useful truth, and challenge without warmth feels like attack.

coreIdeas.mentalMove: A team gets safer and sharper when guidance becomes normal, specific, and two-way. Managers stop saving feedback for formal moments and start correcting course while the work can still improve.
coreIdeas.name: guidance culture
coreIdeas.oneSentence: Guidance means praise and criticism moving in all directions: toward the manager, from the manager, and among peers. The order matters because leaders need to invite criticism before expecting others to receive it.

coreIdeas.mentalMove: A manager who sees growth trajectory avoids treating every ambitious person as superior and every steady expert as stagnant. The team gets both continuity and change without forcing one career script on everyone.
coreIdeas.name: growth trajectory matching
coreIdeas.oneSentence: People need different roles and support depending on whether they are in a steep-growth season or a gradual-growth season. The manager's job is to understand motivation well enough to match opportunity, stability, and challenge to the person.

coreIdeas.mentalMove: Teams move faster when collaboration is structured rather than endless. The wheel shows where work is stuck and prevents leaders from grabbing decisions too early.
coreIdeas.name: GSD Wheel
coreIdeas.oneSentence: The Get Stuff Done Wheel is a seven-step cycle for collaborative execution: Listen, Clarify, Debate, Decide, Persuade, Execute, and Learn. It replaces boss-as-director habits with a process that lets ideas sharpen before action.

coreIdeas.mentalMove: Tools for guidance and results fail when the relationship cannot carry them. Trust routines make future candor less surprising and less threatening.
coreIdeas.name: trust routines
coreIdeas.oneSentence: Relationship-building becomes practical when managers create repeatable routines for trust: staying centered, making time for real conversations, and showing that power is not the only thing moving the relationship.
